title.zh: 卷七十八 列傳第三十八 蕭思話 劉延孫
title.en: Volume 78 Biographies 38: Xiao Sihua, Liu Yansun
title.raw: 卷七十八 列傳第三十八 蕭思話 劉延孫 Volume 78 Biographies 38: Xiao Sihua, Liu Yansun

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十八 蕭思話 劉延孫

translations.literal: Biographies 38: Xiao Sihua, Liu Yansun
translations.idiomatic: Biography 38: Xiao Sihua and Liu Yansun

sentences.zh: 蕭思話，南蘭陵人，孝懿皇后弟子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Sihua was a man of Nanlanling, a younger cousin of Empress Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sihua, a native of Nanlanling, was a nephew of Empress Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 父源之，字君流，歷中書黃門郎，徐、兗二州刺史，冠軍將軍、南琅邪太守。

translations.literal: His father Yuanzhi, styled Junliu, served successively as Secretariat Yellow Gate Attendant, Inspector of Xu and Yan provinces, Champion General, and Administrator of Southern Langye.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiao Yuanzhi, courtesy name Junliu, held posts including Secretariat Yellow Gate Attendant, regional inspector of Xu and Yan, Champion General, and administrator of Southern Langye.

sentences.zh: 永初元年卒，追贈前將軍。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yongchu and was posthumously awarded the rank of Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 420 and was posthumously promoted to Forward General.

sentences.zh: 思話年十許歲，未知書，以博誕遊遨為事，好騎屋棟，打細腰鼓，侵暴鄰曲，莫不患毒之。

translations.literal: When Sihua was about ten years old, he did not yet know books; he made gambling and wild roaming his business, loved riding roof ridges and beating narrow waist drums, and preyed upon neighbors, none of whom did not suffer from his poison.
translations.idiomatic: Around the age of ten, Sihua had not yet learned to read. He spent his days gambling and roaming wild, liked to scamper along roof ridges and beat narrow waist-drums, and bullied the neighbors until they all loathed him.

sentences.zh: 自此折節，數年中，遂有令譽。

translations.literal: From this he reformed his conduct, and within several years he thus gained a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he reformed his ways, and within a few years had earned an excellent name.

sentences.zh: 好書史，善彈琴，能騎射。

translations.literal: He loved books and histories, was skilled at playing the zither, and could ride and shoot.
translations.idiomatic: He took to history and letters, played the zither well, and was capable in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 高祖一見，便以國器許之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, upon a single meeting, then regarded him as material for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu singled him out at first sight as a man fit to serve the state.

sentences.zh: 年十八，除琅邪王大司馬行參軍，轉相國參軍，父憂去職。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he was appointed acting secretary to the Great Marshal of Langye, then transferred to staff officer of the Chancellor of State, and left office on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was made acting secretary on the staff of the Prince of Langye's great marshal, then transferred to a staff post under the chancellor of state; he left office when his father died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，拜羽林監，領石頭戍事，襲爵封陽縣侯，轉宣威將軍、彭城、沛二郡太守。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, charged with garrison affairs at Shitou, inherited the title Marquis of Fengyang County, and was transferred to General Who Displays Might and Administrator of Pengcheng and Pei commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he became supervisor of the imperial guard, took charge of the Shitou garrison, inherited the fief as Marquis of Fengyang, and was promoted to Display Might General and administrator of Pengcheng and Pei.

sentences.zh: 涉獵書傳，頗能隸書，解音律，便弓馬。

translations.literal: He ranged widely in books and records, was quite able in clerical script, understood music, and was adept at bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics, wrote a passable hand in clerical script, understood music theory, and was handy with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 元嘉元年，謝晦為荊州，欲請為司馬，思話拒之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanjia, Xie Hui was in Jingzhou and wished to request him as marshal, but Sihua refused.
translations.idiomatic: In 424, when Xie Hui held Jing province, he tried to recruit Sihua as his chief staff officer; Sihua declined.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷中書侍郎，仍督青州、徐州之東莞諸軍事、振武將軍、青州刺史，時年二十七。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman, and still supervised military affairs of Dongguan in Qing and Xu provinces, as General Who Rouses Might and Inspector of Qing province; he was then twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In 428 he was promoted to secretariat gentleman and appointed to command the Dongguan military district in Qing and Xu, as Rousing Might General and inspector of Qing; he was twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 亡命司馬朗之、元之、可之兄弟，聚黨於東莞發干縣，謀為寇亂。

translations.literal: The outlaw brothers Sima Langzhi, Yuanzhi, and Kezhi gathered a faction at Fagan County in Dongguan and plotted to become bandit rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The fugitive brothers Sima Langzhi, Yuanzhi, and Kezhi raised a band at Fagan in Dongguan and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 思話遣北海太守蕭汪之討斬之，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Sihua sent Beihai Administrator Xiao Wangzhi to attack and behead them, and the remaining faction was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua sent the administrator of Beihai, Xiao Wangzhi, to attack and kill them, and the rest of the band was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 八年，除竟陵王義宣左軍司馬、南沛郡太守。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Left Army Marshal to Prince Jingling Yixuan and Administrator of Nanpei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 431 he became left-army marshal on Prince Jingling Liu Yixuan's staff and administrator of Nanpei.

sentences.zh: 未及就徵，索虜南寇，檀道濟北伐，既而回師，思話懼虜大至，乃棄鎮奔平昌。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the appointment, the Northern Wei barbarians invaded south; Tan Daoji marched north to attack them, then turned his army back. Sihua feared the barbarians would come in great force, and therefore abandoned his post and fled to Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, the Wei crossed the frontier southward. Tan Daoji marched north, then withdrew; fearing a major invasion, Sihua abandoned his command and fled to Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 思話先使參軍劉振之戍下邳，聞思話奔，亦委城走。

translations.literal: Sihua had earlier sent Staff Officer Liu Zhenzhi to garrison Xiapi; hearing that Sihua had fled, he too abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua had earlier posted his aide Liu Zhenzhi at Xiapi; when Liu heard Sihua had fled, he too abandoned the city and ran.

sentences.zh: 虜定不至，而東陽積聚，已為百姓所焚，由是徵下廷尉，仍繫尚方。

translations.literal: The barbarians in the end did not come, but the stored goods at Dongyang had already been burned by the common people; on this account he was summoned down to the Court of Justice and was still imprisoned in the Imperial Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy never appeared, but the supplies stockpiled at Dongyang had been burned by locals. For this he was called to answer before the court of justice and held in the imperial workshops prison.

sentences.zh: 初在青州，常所用銅鬥，覆在藥廚下，得二死雀，思話曰：「鬥覆而雙雀殞，其不祥乎！

translations.literal: Earlier, while in Qing province, the copper dipper he commonly used, overturned under the medicine kitchen, yielded two dead sparrows. Sihua said, "The dipper overturned and twin sparrows perished—is this not ill-omened!
translations.idiomatic: While he was still in Qing province, the copper dipper he used daily was found overturned under the medicine kitchen, with two dead sparrows beneath it. Sihua said, "The dipper overturned and two sparrows died—is this not a bad omen?

sentences.zh: 」既而被繫。

translations.literal: " Shortly after he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 九年，仇池大饑，益、梁州豐稔，梁州刺史甄法護在任失和，氐帥楊難當因此寇漢中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Chouchi suffered great famine, while Yi and Liang provinces had abundant harvests. Liang Inspector Zhen Fahu lost harmony in office, and the Di chieftain Yang Nandang therefore raided Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In 432 Chouchi was stricken by famine while Yi and Liang enjoyed good harvests. Zhen Fahu, inspector of Liang, had lost control of his command, and the Di leader Yang Nandang seized the chance to invade Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 乃自徒中起思話督梁、南秦二州諸軍事、橫野將軍、梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon from among the convicts Sihua was raised to supervise the military affairs of Liang and Southern Qin provinces, as General Who Sweeps the Wilderness and Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua was then released from prison and appointed to command the armies of Liang and Southern Qin, as Sweeping Wilderness General and inspector of both provinces.

sentences.zh: 既行，聞法護已委鎮北奔西城，遣司馬、建威將軍、南漢中太守蕭諱五百人前進；

translations.literal: Once on the march, hearing that Fahu had abandoned his post and fled north to Xicheng, he sent Marshal, General Who Establishes Might, and Administrator of Southern Hanzhong Xiao Hui forward with five hundred men;
translations.idiomatic: On the march he learned that Fahu had abandoned his post and fled north to Xicheng. He sent his marshal Xiao Hui—Display Might General and administrator of Southern Hanzhong—ahead with five hundred men;

sentences.zh: 又遣西戎長史蕭汪之係之。

translations.literal: and also sent Western Rong Chief Clerk Xiao Wangzhi to bring up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: and sent chief clerk for the western tribes Xiao Wangzhi to follow in support.

sentences.zh: 諱緣路收合士眾，得精兵千人。

translations.literal: Hui along the route gathered soldiers and masses, obtaining a thousand elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: Along the route Hui rallied troops and mustered a thousand picked soldiers.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，進據磝頭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year he advanced and occupied Qiaotou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 433 he advanced and took Qiaotou.

sentences.zh: 難當焚掠漢中，引眾西還，留其輔國將軍、梁秦二州刺史趙溫守梁州，魏興太守薛健據黃金。

translations.literal: Nandang burned and plundered Hanzhong, led his masses westward back, left his Assisting State General and Inspector of Liang and Qin Zhao Wen to guard Liang province, and Weixing Administrator Xue Jian held Huangjin.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang burned and looted Hanzhong, then withdrew west, leaving his Assisting State General and joint inspector of Liang and Qin, Zhao Wen, to hold Liang province while Weixing administrator Xue Jian occupied Huangjin.

sentences.zh: 諱進屯磝頭，遣陰平太守蕭坦赴黃金，薛健副薑寶據鐵城，鐵城與黃金相對，去一裏，斫樹塞道。

translations.literal: Hui advanced and encamped at Qiaotou, sent Yinping Administrator Xiao Tan toward Huangjin; Xue Jian's deputy Jiang Bao held Tiecheng. Tiecheng and Huangjin faced each other, one li apart; they felled trees to block the road.
translations.idiomatic: Hui moved up to Qiaotou and sent Yinping administrator Xiao Tan against Huangjin. Xue Jian's lieutenant Jiang Bao held Tiecheng, a mile across from Huangjin, with the road blocked by felled trees.

sentences.zh: 坦進攻二戍，拔之。

translations.literal: Tan advanced to attack the two garrisons and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Tan attacked both strongpoints and took them.

sentences.zh: 二月，趙溫又率薛健及其寧朔將軍、馮翼太守蒲早子來攻坦營，坦奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: In the second month Zhao Wen again led Xue Jian and his Pacifying the North General and Administrator of Fengyi Pu Zaozi to attack Tan's camp; Tan fought fiercely and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Zhao Wen led Xue Jian and Pu Zaozi—Pacifying the North General and administrator of Fengyi—against Tan's camp. Tan struck hard and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 坦被創，賊退保西水。

translations.literal: Tan was wounded; the rebels withdrew to hold Xishui.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was wounded in the fight, and the enemy fell back to defend Xishui.

sentences.zh: 諱司馬錫文祖進據黃金，蕭汪之步騎五百相繼而至。

translations.literal: Hui's marshal Xi Wenzu advanced to occupy Huangjin, and Xiao Wangzhi's five hundred infantry and cavalry arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's marshal Xi Wenzu moved into Huangjin, and Xiao Wangzhi came up with five hundred foot and horse in succession.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍臨川王義慶遣龍驤將軍裴方明三千人赴，諱等進黃金，早子、健等退保下桃。

translations.literal: Pacifying West General Prince Linchuan Yiqing sent Dragon Cavalry General Pei Fangming with three thousand men to the relief; Hui and the others advanced on Huangjin, and Zaozi, Jian, and the rest withdrew to hold Xiatao.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Linchuan Liu Yiqing, Pacifying West General, sent Dragon Cavalry General Pei Fangming with three thousand men. Hui pressed on to Huangjin, and Zaozi and Jian fell back to Xiatao.

sentences.zh: 思話先遣行參軍王靈濟率偏軍出洋川，因向南城。

translations.literal: Sihua had earlier sent Acting Staff Officer Wang Lingji leading a detached army out through Yangchuan, and thereby south toward Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua had already sent acting staff officer Wang Lingji with a detached force through Yangchuan toward Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 偽陵江將軍趙英堅守險，靈濟擊破之，生禽英。

translations.literal: The false Crossing-the-River General Zhao Ying held fast in the defiles; Lingji attacked and routed him, taking Ying alive.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy general Zhao Ying, Crossing-the-River General, held the passes. Lingji broke him and took Ying alive.

sentences.zh: 南城空虛，因資無所，復引軍還與諱合。

translations.literal: Nancheng was empty; there was nowhere to draw supplies, so he again led his army back to join Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Nancheng was empty and offered no supplies, so he turned back and rejoined Hui.

sentences.zh: 三月，諱率眾軍進據峨公固。

translations.literal: In the third month Hui led the mass of armies forward to occupy Egonggu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Hui led the main force to Egonggu.

sentences.zh: 難當遣其子和率趙溫、蒲早子及左衛將軍呂平、寧朔將軍司馬飛龍，步騎萬餘，跨漢津結柴，其間立浮橋，悉力攻諱，合圍數十重，短兵接戰，弓矢無復用。

translations.literal: Nandang sent his son He leading Zhao Wen, Pu Zaozi, Left Guard General Lü Ping, and Pacifying the North General Sima Feilong, with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry. They crossed the Han ford, built stockades, set a pontoon bridge between them, and with full force attacked Hui, surrounding him in dozens of rings; at close quarters they fought hand to hand, and bows and arrows were no longer of use.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang sent his son He at the head of Zhao Wen, Pu Zaozi, Left Guard General Lü Ping, and Pacifying the North General Sima Feilong, with over ten thousand foot and horse. They crossed the Han, threw up stockades and a pontoon bridge between them, and threw everything at Hui in layer upon layer of encirclement until the fight came to blades at close range and bows were useless.

sentences.zh: 賊悉衣犀革，戈矛所不能加。

translations.literal: The rebels all wore rhinoceros hide, and spears and halberds could not pierce them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy all wore rhinoceros-hide armor that spears and halberds could not penetrate.

sentences.zh: 諱乃截矟長數尺，以大斧椎之，一矟輒貫十餘賊。

translations.literal: Hui then cut spears to several feet in length, drove them with great axes, and one spear would pierce through more than ten rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had spears cut to several feet and driven in with heavy axes; a single thrust would run through more than ten men.

sentences.zh: 賊不能當，因大敗，燒柴奔走，退據大桃。

translations.literal: The rebels could not withstand it and were therefore greatly defeated; they burned the stockades and fled, withdrawing to hold Datao.
translations.idiomatic: They could not stand against this and broke in rout, burning their stockades as they fled to Datao.

sentences.zh: 閏月，諱及方明臺軍至，龍驤將軍楊平興、幢主殿中將軍梁坦直入角弩追之，賊又敗走，殺傷虜獲甚多。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month Hui and Fangming's allied armies arrived; Dragon Cavalry General Yang Pingxing and Pennant Commander Palace General Liang Tan pressed in with crossbows and pursued; the rebels were again defeated and fled, with many killed, wounded, captured, and taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Hui was joined by Pei Fangming's allied troops. Dragon Cavalry General Yang Pingxing and pennant commander Palace General Liang Tan pressed the pursuit with crossbows. The enemy broke again, leaving heavy casualties and captures.

sentences.zh: 漢中平，悉收沒地，置戍葭萌水。

translations.literal: Hanzhong was pacified; all lost territory was recovered, and a garrison was set at Jiameng Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong was pacified, lost ground recovered, and a garrison established at Jiameng Ford.

sentences.zh: 先是，桓玄篡晉，以桓希為梁州。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huan Xuan usurped Jin, he appointed Huan Xi as Inspector of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Huan Xuan seized the Jin throne, he had appointed Huan Xi inspector of Liang.

sentences.zh: 布敗走，氐楊盛據有漢中，刺史范元之、傅歆悉治魏興，唯得魏興、上庸、新城三郡。

translations.literal: Bu was defeated and fled; the Di Yang Sheng seized Hanzhong. Inspectors Fan Yuanzhi and Fu Xin both administered from Weixing, obtaining only the three commanderies of Weixing, Shangyong, and Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Bu was defeated and fled, the Di leader Yang Sheng held Hanzhong. Inspectors Fan Yuanzhi and Fu Xin governed only from Weixing, retaining just Weixing, Shangyong, and Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 其後索邈為刺史，乃治南城。

translations.literal: Afterward Suo Miao became inspector and then administered from Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Suo Miao became inspector, the seat was moved to Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 為賊所焚燒不可固，即思話遷鎮南域，加節，進號寧朔將軍，征諱為太子屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: It had been burned by rebels and could not be held firm; thereupon Sihua moved his headquarters to the southern region, was granted the staff of authority, advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the North, and summoned Hui as Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Because it had been burned by the enemy and could not be held, Sihua moved his headquarters to the southern region, received the staff of command, was promoted to Pacifying the North General, and recalled Hui as colonel of the heir apparent's garrison cavalry.

sentences.zh: 法護，中山無極人，過江寓居南郡。

translations.literal: Fahu was a man of Wuji in Zhongshan; crossing the river he lodged in Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fahu was from Wuji in Zhongshan and, after crossing south, had settled in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 弟法崇，元嘉十年，自少府為益州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Fachong, in the tenth year of Yuanjia, went from Minister Steward to Inspector of Yi province.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fachong became inspector of Yi in 433, transferred from the minister steward's office.

sentences.zh: 法護委鎮之罪，統府所收，於獄賜死。

translations.literal: For Fahu's crime of abandoning his post, the headquarters confiscated his property, and he was granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Fahu was condemned for abandoning his post; his property was seized by the headquarters, and he was ordered to take his own life in prison.

sentences.zh: 太祖以法崇受任一方，令獄官言法護病卒。

translations.literal: The Taizu, because Fachong held appointment in a region, ordered the prison officials to say that Fahu had died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fachong held a provincial command, the Taizu had the prison authorities report that Fahu had died of illness.

sentences.zh: 太祖使思話上平定漢中本末，下之史官。

translations.literal: The Taizu had Sihua submit the full account of pacifying Hanzhong and sent it down to the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu had Sihua submit a full report on the pacification of Hanzhong for the court historians.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷使持節、臨川王義慶平西長史、南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred as Bearer of the Staff, Chief Clerk for Pacifying the West under Prince Linchuan Yiqing, and Colonel of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: In 437 he became bearer of the staff, chief clerk for Pacifying the West on Prince Linchuan's staff, and colonel of the southern tribes.

sentences.zh: 太祖賜以弓琴，手敕曰：「丈人頃何所作？

translations.literal: The Taizu bestowed a bow and zither upon him, with a personal edict saying, "Elder, what have you been doing lately?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu sent him a bow and a zither with a personal note: "My dear sir, what have you been up to lately?

sentences.zh: 事務之暇，故以琴書為娛耳，所得不曰義邪！

translations.literal: In the leisure from affairs, you therefore take zither and books for amusement—is what you gain not called righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: In your spare hours from office you amuse yourself with zither and books—is that not a worthy use of time?

sentences.zh: 眷想常不忘情，想亦同之。

translations.literal: My affectionate thoughts constantly do not forget feeling; I think you feel the same.
translations.idiomatic: I think of you often and trust you feel the same.

sentences.zh: 前得此琴，云是舊物，亦有名京邑，今以相借。

translations.literal: Earlier I obtained this zither, said to be an old object, also famous in the capital; now I lend it to you.
translations.idiomatic: I recently acquired this zither, said to be an old instrument once celebrated in the capital, and now lend it to you.

sentences.zh: 因是戴顒意於彈撫，響韻殊勝，直爾嘉也。

translations.literal: Because Dai Yong took pleasure in playing it, its tone and resonance are especially superior—truly admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yong enjoyed playing it; the tone is exceptionally fine, and I thought you would appreciate it.

sentences.zh: 並往桑弓一張，材理乃快，先所常用，既久廢射，又多病，略不能制之，便成老公，令人歎息。

translations.literal: Also sent is one mulberry bow; its grain and texture are keen—it was what I commonly used before. Having long abandoned shooting, and being much afflicted by illness, I can scarcely control it anymore and have become an old man, which makes one sigh.
translations.idiomatic: I also send a mulberry-wood bow of excellent grain that I once used constantly. I have long since given up archery, and illness has left me barely able to draw it—I have become an old man, which is lamentable.

sentences.zh: 良材美器，宜在盡用之地，丈人真無所與讓也。」

translations.literal: Fine timber and beautiful instruments ought to be where they are fully used; Elder, you truly have no one to yield to."
translations.idiomatic: Good wood and fine instruments belong where they will be fully used; my dear sir, you need not stand on ceremony."

sentences.zh: 十六年，衡陽王義季代義慶，又除安西長史，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Prince Hengyang Yiji replaced Yiqing, and he was again appointed Chief Clerk for Pacifying the West, the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 439, when Prince Hengyang Liu Yiji replaced Yiqing, Sihua was again made chief clerk for Pacifying the West; his other titles were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 十九年，徵為侍中，領前軍將軍，未就徵，復先職。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Forward General of the Vanguard; he did not take up the summons and returned to his former posts.
translations.idiomatic: In 442 he was summoned as attendant-in-ordinary and commander of the vanguard army, but before he could take up the appointment he was restored to his former posts.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷持節、監雍州、梁、南北秦四州、荊州之南陽、竟陵、順陽、襄陽、新野、隨六郡諸軍事、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史、襄陽太守。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred as Bearer of the Staff, overseer of Yong, Liang, and the two Qins north and south, military affairs of the six Jing commanderies of Nanyang, Jingling, Shunyang, Xiangyang, Xinye, and Sui, Colonel Who Pacifies the Man, Inspector of Yong, and Administrator of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became bearer of the staff, overseer of Yong, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin, commander of the six Jing commanderies from Nanyang through Sui, colonel who pacifies the tribes, inspector of Yong, and administrator of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，除侍中，領太子右率。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Right Leader of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In 445 he was made attendant-in-ordinary and right leader of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，改領左衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was changed to concurrently Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In 447 he was reassigned as left guard general.

sentences.zh: 嘗從太祖登鍾山北嶺，中道有磐石清泉，上使於石上彈琴，因賜以銀鍾酒，謂曰：「相賞有松石間意。

translations.literal: Once he followed the Taizu up the northern ridge of Zhongshan; midway there was a boulder and clear spring. The sovereign had him play the zither on the stone and thereupon bestowed silver-bell wine, saying, "Mutual appreciation has the mood of pines and rocks.
translations.idiomatic: Once, accompanying the Taizu up the north ridge of Zhongshan, they came to a boulder beside a clear spring. The emperor had him play the zither on the rock and gave him silver-bell wine, saying, "This is the pleasure of pines and stones together.

sentences.zh: 」又領南徐州大中正。

translations.literal: " He also concurrently held Grand Rectifier of Southern Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: " He also served as grand rectifier of Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 明年，復監雍、梁、南北秦四州、荊州之竟陵、隨二郡諸軍事、右將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史如故。

translations.literal: The next year he again oversaw Yong, Liang, and the two Qins north and south, military affairs of the two Jing commanderies of Jingling and Sui, as Right General, Colonel Who Pacifies the Man, and Inspector of Yong, as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he resumed oversight of Yong, Liang, Northern and Southern Qin, and the Jing commanderies of Jingling and Sui, as right general, colonel who pacifies the tribes, and inspector of Yong, as before.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，徵為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was summoned as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 449 he was summoned to head the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 詔思話曰：「沈尚書暴病不救，其體業貞審，立朝盡公，年時尚可，方相委任，奄忽不永，痛惋特深。

translations.literal: An edict to Sihua said, "Minister Shen's sudden illness could not be saved. His person and conduct were upright and careful; in court he was wholly public-minded. His years were still suitable, and we were just about to entrust him further—suddenly he was not long-lived; the pain and regret are especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to Sihua read: "Minister Shen's sudden illness proved fatal. Upright in person and careful in conduct, wholly devoted in office, he was still in his prime and we had meant to rely on him further. His sudden death grieves us deeply.

sentences.zh: 銓管要機，通塞所寄，丈人才用體國，二三惟允。

translations.literal: The evaluation and control of crucial posts is what blockage and passage depend upon; Elder's talent and capacity embrace the state—of two or three men, you alone are fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The evaluation of key appointments is vital to the realm's fortunes; your talent serves the state, and of the few men fit for this post you are foremost."

sentences.zh: 」思話以去州無復事力，倩府軍身九人，太祖戲之曰：「丈人終不為田父于裏閭，何應無人使邪？

translations.literal: " Sihua, because leaving the province left him without administrative staff, requested nine men from the princely establishment's military household. The Taizu jested with him, saying, "Elder will after all not be a farmer in the lanes—how should you have no one to attend you?
translations.idiomatic: Sihua, having left his province without household staff, asked for nine attendants from the princely establishment. The Taizu teased him: "Surely you are not to become a village farmer in the lanes—how can you have no servants?

sentences.zh: 」未拜，二十七年，遷護軍將軍。

translations.literal: " Before he took up the appointment, in the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: " Before he could take office, in 450 he was made general of the guards.

sentences.zh: 是年春，虜攻懸瓠，太祖將大舉北討，朝士僉同，莫或異議。

translations.literal: That spring the barbarians attacked Xuanchi; the Taizu was about to launch a great northern campaign. Court gentlemen were all of one mind, none dissenting.
translations.idiomatic: That spring the Wei attacked Xuanchi. The Taizu planned a major northern campaign, and the court was unanimous—no one dissented.

sentences.zh: 思話固諫，不從。

translations.literal: Sihua firmly remonstrated; he was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua argued strongly against it but was overruled.

sentences.zh: 乃領精甲三千，助鎮彭城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led three thousand picked armored troops to assist in garrisoning Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then led three thousand picked troops to help hold Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 虜退，即代世祖為持節、監徐、兗、青、冀四州、豫州之梁郡諸軍事、撫軍將軍、兗、徐二州刺史。

translations.literal: When the barbarians withdrew, he immediately replaced the Shizu as Bearer of the Staff, overseer of Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji provinces and military affairs of Liang commandery in Yu, as Pacifying Army General and Inspector of Yan and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew, he replaced the future Emperor Xiaowu as bearer of the staff, commander of Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji and of Liang commandery in Yu, as pacifying army general and inspector of Yan and Xu.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，統揚武將軍、冀州刺史張永眾軍圍碻磝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he commanded the mass of armies under Rousing Might General and Inspector of Ji Zhang Yong to besiege Quebi.
translations.idiomatic: In 452 he took overall command of Zhang Yong's forces—Rousing Might General and inspector of Ji—in the siege of Quebi.

sentences.zh: 初，鎮軍諮議參軍申坦與王玄謨圍滑臺，不克，免官。

translations.literal: Earlier, Army-quelling Adviser Staff Officer Shen Tan and Wang Xuamo had besieged Huatai without success and were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, army-quelling adviser Shen Tan had joined Wang Xuamo in the unsuccessful siege of Huatai and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史蕭斌板坦行建威將軍、濟南平原二郡太守，守歷城，令任仲仁又為坦副，並前鋒入河。

translations.literal: Qing Inspector Xiao Bin commissioned Tan as acting General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Jinan and Pingyuan, to guard Licheng; he ordered Ren Zhongren again as Tan's deputy, and both advanced as vanguard into the Yellow River region.
translations.idiomatic: Qing inspector Xiao Bin reinstated Tan as acting Display Might General and administrator of Jinan and Pingyuan, posted him at Licheng, and made Ren Zhongren his deputy; both led the vanguard into the river frontier.

sentences.zh: 五月，發沿口，永司馬崔訓、建武將軍齊郡太守胡景世率青州軍來會。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they set out from Yankou; Yong's marshal Cui Xun and Establishing Martial General and Administrator of Qi commandery Hu Jingshi led Qing army troops to join.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they marched from Yankou. Zhang Yong's marshal Cui Xun and Display Martial General Hu Jingshi, administrator of Qi, brought the Qing forces to the rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 七月，思話及眾軍並至碻磝，治三攻道。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Sihua and the mass of armies all reached Quebi and constructed three assault approaches.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Sihua and the allied armies reached Quebi and opened three assault trenches.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣員外散騎侍郎徐爰宣旨督戰。

translations.literal: The Taizu sent Extraordinary Gentleman Attendant-at-Large Xu Ai to proclaim the imperial will and supervise the battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu sent extraordinary attendant Xu Ai with imperial orders to oversee the fighting.

sentences.zh: 張永、胡景世當東攻道，申坦、任仲仁西攻道，崔訓南攻道。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong and Hu Jingshi took the eastern assault approach; Shen Tan and Ren Zhongren the western; Cui Xun the southern.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong and Hu Jingshi held the eastern approach, Shen Tan and Ren Zhongren the western, and Cui Xun the southern.

sentences.zh: 賊夜地道出，燒崔訓樓及蟆車，又燒胡景世樓及攻具，尋又毀崔訓攻道，城不可拔。

translations.literal: The rebels came out by tunnel at night, burned Cui Xun's tower and siege vehicles, also burned Hu Jingshi's tower and assault equipment, and soon afterward destroyed Cui Xun's assault approach; the city could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders sallied by night through tunnels, burned Cui Xun's tower and siege engines, then Hu Jingshi's tower and equipment, and finally wrecked Cui Xun's approach. The city could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 思話馳來，退師。

translations.literal: Sihua came at full speed and withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua rode up in haste and ordered a withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 攻城凡十八日，解圍還歷下。

translations.literal: The siege of the city lasted eighteen days in all; they lifted the encirclement and returned to Lixia.
translations.idiomatic: After eighteen days of siege they raised the blockade and withdrew to Lixia.

sentences.zh: 崔訓以樓見燒，又不能固攻道，被誅於碻磝；

translations.literal: Cui Xun, because his tower was burned and he could not secure the assault approach, was executed at Quebi;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xun was executed at Quebi because his tower had been burned and he had failed to hold his approach;

sentences.zh: 永、坦並繫獄。

translations.literal: Yong and Tan were both imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong and Shen Tan were both imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「得撫軍將軍思話啟事，碻磝不拔，士卒疲勞，且班師清濟，更圖進討。

translations.literal: An edict said, "We have received Pacifying Army General Sihua's memorial: Quebi could not be taken, the soldiers are weary, and for the present the army is withdrawn to clear the Ji River and plan a renewed advance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Pacifying Army General Sihua reports that Quebi could not be taken, the troops are exhausted, and the army is withdrawn to the clear Ji to plan a new advance.

sentences.zh: 此鎮山川嚴阻，控臨河朔，形勝之要，擅名自古，宜除其授，以允望實。

translations.literal: This fortress has stern mountains and barriers, overlooks the north of the Yellow River, and is a strategic point famous from antiquity; its appointment should be removed to match expectation and reality.
translations.idiomatic: This fortress lies in rugged terrain commanding the north bank of the Yellow River—a famous strategic post since antiquity. Its command should be reorganized to match the need.

sentences.zh: 思話可解徐州為冀州，餘如故。

translations.literal: Sihua may relinquish Xu province for Ji province; the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua is to exchange Xu for Ji province; his other titles remain.

sentences.zh: 彭城文武，復量分配，即鎮歷城。

translations.literal: Pengcheng's civil and military personnel are to be reassigned in due measure, and he is immediately to garrison Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military staff at Pengcheng are to be redistributed, and he is to take up headquarters at Licheng at once.

sentences.zh: 」尋為江夏王義恭所奏，免官。

translations.literal: " Soon he was memorialized by Prince Jiangxia Yigong and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Prince Jiangxia Liu Yigong memorialized against him, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 元兇弑立，以為使持節、監徐、青、兗、冀四州、豫州之梁郡諸軍事、徐、兗二州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When the usurper murdered and enthroned himself, he appointed him Bearer of the Staff, overseer of Xu, Qing, Yan, and Ji and military affairs of Liang commandery in Yu, Inspector of Xu and Yan, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the usurper Liu Shao seized the throne by regicide, he reappointed Sihua bearer of the staff, commander of Xu, Qing, Yan, and Ji and of Liang in Yu, and inspector of Xu and Yan, with his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 思話即率部曲還彭城，起義以應世祖。

translations.literal: Sihua immediately led his household troops back to Pengcheng and raised righteous arms to respond to the Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua at once led his personal forces back to Pengcheng and rose in support of the future Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 遣使奉箋曰：「下官近在歷下，始奉國諱，所承使人，不知闊狹，既還在路，漸有所聞，猶謂人倫無容有此，私懷感慨，未敢在言。

translations.literal: He sent envoys with a written submission saying, "Your subordinate was recently at Lixia and had just received the national mourning taboo. The envoy I received did not know breadth or narrowness; once back on the road I gradually heard something, yet still thought human relations could not contain this. In private I harbored emotion and did not dare speak openly.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys with a memorial: "Your servant was recently at Lixia when the national mourning was proclaimed. The messenger I received gave no clear account; only on the road back did I gradually hear rumors, and I still could not believe that human relations could permit such a thing. I kept my grief private and dared not speak openly.

sentences.zh: 奉被今教，果出慮表，重增哀惋，不能自勝。

translations.literal: Receiving your present instruction, it has indeed exceeded what I feared; my grief and regret are redoubled, and I cannot overcome myself.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have received your present command, the truth is worse than I had feared. My grief is redoubled beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 此實天地所不覆載，人神所不容忍，率土民氓，莫不憤咽，況下官蒙荷榮渥，義兼常志。

translations.literal: This truly is what heaven and earth do not cover and bear, what men and spirits cannot endure; all the people within the realm, none fail to choke with rage—how much more your subordinate, who has received honored grace, with duty beyond ordinary resolve.
translations.idiomatic: This is an outrage that heaven and earth cannot shelter and that gods and men cannot abide. Every subject under heaven chokes with rage—how much more your servant, who has received such grace and owes a duty beyond the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 此月五日，被驛使追命騎還朝，切齒拊心，輒已鍾疾，雖百口在都，一非所顧。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of this month, pursued by post-riders, he was ordered to return to court by mounted escort. Gnashing his teeth and striking his breast, illness at once seized him. Though a hundred mouths were in the capital, not one was his concern.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth of this month post-riders summoned me back to court by forced march. I gnashed my teeth and clutched my heart until illness seized me at once. Though a hundred kinsmen remain in the capital, not one of them could hold me back.

sentences.zh: 正欲遣啟受規略，會奉今旨，悲懼兼情。

translations.literal: He had just intended to send a memorial to receive strategy, when he met the present order—grief and fear mingled in feeling.
translations.idiomatic: I was about to send a memorial asking for your plan of campaign when your present command arrived, and grief and fear overwhelmed me together.

sentences.zh: 伏承司徒英圖電發，殿下神武霜斷，臧質忠義並到，不謀同時，仗順沿流，席捲江甸，前驅風邁，已應在近。

translations.literal: I humbly learn that the Minister over the Masses's heroic plan flashes like lightning, Your Highness's divine martial resolve cuts like frost, Zang Zhi's loyalty and righteousness have both arrived without plotting at the same moment—relying on righteousness flowing downstream, sweeping the Jiang region; the vanguard's wind is swift and should be near already.
translations.idiomatic: I learn that the Minister over the Masses has launched his plan like lightning, that Your Highness's divine martial resolve strikes like frost, and that Zang Zhi has brought his loyal forces—all acting in concert without prior conspiracy, riding the tide of righteousness downriver to sweep the Jiang region. Your vanguard must already be near.

sentences.zh: 下官復練始集，遣輔國將軍申坦、龍驤將軍梁坦二軍，分配精甲五千，申坦為統，便以即日水陸齊下。

translations.literal: Your subordinate has again gathered the newly trained troops and dispatched the two armies of Assisting State General Shen Tan and Dragon Cavalry General Liang Tan, assigning five thousand picked armored troops with Shen Tan as commander-in-chief, to set out this very day by land and water together downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has mustered his newly drilled troops and dispatched the armies of Assisting State General Shen Tan and Dragon Cavalry General Liang Tan with five thousand picked armored men under Shen Tan's overall command, to march downstream by land and water this very day.

sentences.zh: 下官悉率文武，駱驛繼發。

translations.literal: Your subordinate will lead all civil and military personnel in relay, posting at full speed.
translations.idiomatic: I shall lead all my civil and military officers in rapid succession behind them.

sentences.zh: 憑威策懦，勢同振朽，開泰有期，悲欣交集。

translations.literal: Relying on prestige to strike cowards, the momentum is like shaking rotten wood; the opening of peace has its term—grief and joy intermingle.
translations.idiomatic: With your prestige driving cowards before us, the enemy will crumble like rotten wood. The restoration draws near, and my grief and joy are mingled.

sentences.zh: 」世祖至新亭，坦亦進克京口。

translations.literal: " The Shizu reached Xinting; Tan also advanced and captured Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: " When the future Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting, Liang Tan also advanced and took Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian he died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 465, at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 追贈征西將軍、開府儀同三司，持節、常侍、都督、刺史如故，諡曰穆侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General Who Conquers the West, Grand Marshal with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, staff of authority, regular attendant, overseer, and inspector as before; posthumous title Marquis Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Conquering West General and grand marshal with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, retaining the staff, regular attendant, overseer, and inspector titles; his posthumous name was Marquis Mu.

sentences.zh: 思話宗戚令望，蚤見任待，凡歷州十二，杖節監都督九焉。

translations.literal: Sihua came of distinguished clan and repute, was early given trust and favor, holding twelve provinces in all and bearing the staff as overseer and commander nine times.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua came from a clan of standing and was trusted early in life. He governed twelve provinces in all and nine times bore the staff as overseer or commander.

sentences.zh: 所至雖無皦皦清節，亦無穢黷之累。

translations.literal: Wherever he went, though he had no brilliantly pure integrity, he also had no stain of corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Nowhere he served did he earn a reputation for spotless integrity, but neither was he tainted by corruption.

sentences.zh: 愛才好士，人多歸之。

translations.literal: He loved talent and honored scholars; many men attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and honored scholars, and many men gathered to him.

sentences.zh: 長子惠開嗣，別有傳。

translations.literal: His eldest son Hui'kai succeeded him; his biography is given separately.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Hui'kai succeeded him; his biography appears elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 次子惠明，亦有世譽，歷黃門郎，御史中丞，司徒左長史，吳興太守。

translations.literal: His second son Huiming also had a reputation in the age, serving as Yellow Gate Attendant, Censor-in-Chief, Left Chief Clerk of the Minister over the Masses, and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Huiming also enjoyed a fine reputation, serving as yellow gate attendant, censor-in-chief, left chief clerk to the minister over the masses, and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽末，卒官。

translations.literal: In the final year of Emperor Houfei of Yuanhui, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the end of the Yuanhui era under Emperor Houfei.

sentences.zh: 第四子惠基，順帝昇明末，為侍中。

translations.literal: His fourth son Huiji, at the end of Emperor Shundi's Shengming reign, was Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His fourth son Huiji became attendant-in-ordinary at the end of Emperor Shundi's Shengming reign.

sentences.zh: 源之從父弟摹之，丹陽尹，追贈征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi's younger male cousin by the father's line Mozhi was Governor of Danyang and was posthumously awarded General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi's paternal cousin Mozhi served as governor of Danyang and was posthumously made Punishing Barbarians General.

sentences.zh: 子斌，亦為太祖所遇。

translations.literal: His son Bin was also favored by the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin was likewise favored by the Taizu.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康鎮豫章，以為大將軍諮議參軍、豫章太守。

translations.literal: When Prince Pengcheng Yikang governed Yuzhang, he was made Grand Marshal Adviser Staff Officer and Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Pengcheng Liu Yikang governed Yuzhang, Bin was made grand marshal adviser and administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 歷南蠻校尉，侍中，輔國將軍、青冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: He held Colonel of the Southern Man, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Assisting State General with Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as colonel of the southern tribes, attendant-in-ordinary, assisting state general, and inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，統王玄謨等眾軍北伐。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he commanded the mass of armies under Wang Xuamo on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In 450 he took overall command of Wang Xuamo's forces on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 斌遣將軍崔猛攻虜青州刺史張淮之於樂安，淮之棄城走。

translations.literal: Bin sent General Cui Meng to attack the barbarians' Qing Inspector Zhang Huaizhi at Le'an; Huaizhi abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Bin sent General Cui Meng against the Wei Qing inspector Zhang Huaizhi at Le'an; Huaizhi abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 先是，猛與斌參軍傅融分取樂安及碻磝，樂安水道不通，先並定碻磝，至是又克樂安。

translations.literal: Earlier, Meng and Bin's staff officer Fu Rong had divided the taking of Le'an and Quebi; Le'an's waterways were not passable, so they first together secured Quebi; by this time they also captured Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Meng and Bin's aide Fu Rong had been assigned to take Le'an and Quebi separately. Because Le'an's waterways were blocked, they secured Quebi first and only now also took Le'an.

sentences.zh: 既而攻圍滑臺，不拔。

translations.literal: Thereafter they attacked and besieged Huatai but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: They then besieged Huatai but failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 斌追還歷下，事在王玄謨傳。

translations.literal: Bin pursued back to Lixia; the account is in Wang Xuamo's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Bin withdrew to Lixia; the full account is in Wang Xuamo's biography.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，亡命司馬順則詐稱晉室近屬，自號齊王，聚眾據梁鄒城。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the outlaw Sima Shunze falsely claimed to be a close kinsman of the Jin house, styled himself King of Qi, gathered a host, and seized Liangzou city.
translations.idiomatic: In 451 the fugitive Sima Shunze falsely claimed kinship with the Jin imperial house, proclaimed himself King of Qi, and raised a band to hold Liangzou.

sentences.zh: 又有沙門自稱司馬百年，號安定王，亡命秦凱之、祖元明等各據村屯以應順則。

translations.literal: There was also a monk who called himself Sima Bainian, styled King of Anding; the outlaws Qin Kaizhi, Zu Yuanming, and others each held village stockades in response to Shunze.
translations.idiomatic: A monk also called himself Sima Bainian and styled himself King of Anding, while fugitives Qin Kaizhi, Zu Yuanming, and others seized village strongholds in support of Shunze.

sentences.zh: 初，梁鄒戍主、宣威將軍、樂安、渤海二郡太守崔勳之出州，故順則因虛竊據。

translations.literal: Earlier, the garrison commander of Liangzou, General Who Displays Might, and Administrator of Le'an and Bohai Cui Xunzhi had left the province, so Shunze took advantage of the vacancy to seize it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liangzou's garrison commander Cui Xunzhi—Display Might General and administrator of Le'an and Bohai—had left the province, Shunze seized the chance to occupy the city.

sentences.zh: 勳之司馬曹敬會拒戰不敵，出走。

translations.literal: Xunzhi's marshal Cao Jinghui resisted battle but could not match them and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhi's marshal Cao Jinghui fought but was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 斌即遣勳之率行建威將軍濟南、平原二郡太守申坦、長流參軍羅文昌等諸軍討順則，攻之不克。

translations.literal: Bin immediately sent Xunzhi leading Acting General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Jinan and Pingyuan Shen Tan, Chief Clerk for Long Campaign Luo Wenchang, and the various armies to punish Shunze; they attacked but could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Bin at once sent Xunzhi with acting Display Might General and administrator of Jinan and Pingyuan Shen Tan, campaign chief clerk Luo Wenchang, and their forces against Shunze, but the assault failed.

sentences.zh: 勳之等始謂城內出於逼附，軍至即應奔逃，而並為賊堅守，殺傷官軍甚多。

translations.literal: Xunzhi and the others at first thought those inside the city had joined under compulsion and would flee once the army arrived, but all firmly held for the rebels and killed or wounded many government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhi and his men had assumed the townspeople had joined under duress and would flee when the army arrived, but the rebels held firm and inflicted heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 斌又遣府司馬、建武將軍、齊郡太守龐秀之總諸軍。

translations.literal: Bin again sent Princely Marshal, Establishing Martial General, and Administrator of Qi commandery Pang Xiuzhi to command the mass of armies.
translations.idiomatic: Bin then sent his princely marshal Pang Xiuzhi—Display Martial General and administrator of Qi—to take overall command.

sentences.zh: 祖元明又據安丘城，斌更遣振武將軍劉武之及軍主劉回精兵千人，討司馬百年，斬之。

translations.literal: Zu Yuanming again held Anciu city; Bin further sent Rousing Might General Liu Wuzhi and Army Commander Liu Hui with a thousand picked troops to punish Sima Bainian and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Yuanming also seized Anciu, Bin sent Rousing Might General Liu Wuzhi and army commander Liu Hui with a thousand picked men against Sima Bainian and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 順則既失據，眾稍離阻。

translations.literal: Once Shunze had lost his foothold, the masses gradually dispersed and obstructed one another.
translations.idiomatic: With Shunze's base lost, his followers began to scatter.

sentences.zh: 文昌遣道連偽投賊，賊信納之，潛以官賞格示眾，城內賊黨李繼叔等並有歸順心。

translations.literal: Wenchang sent Dao Lian to feign surrender to the rebels; the rebels trusted and accepted him. Secretly he showed the crowd the government's reward schedule; within the city the rebel faction Li Jishu and others all had hearts inclined to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang sent Dao Lian to infiltrate the rebels, who accepted him. He secretly circulated the government's reward schedule, and men inside such as Li Jishu began to waver toward surrender.

sentences.zh: 道連謀泄，為賊所殺，繼叔逾城出降，賊黨於是大離。

translations.literal: Dao Lian's plot was exposed and he was killed by the rebels; Jishu climbed over the wall to surrender, and the rebel faction thereupon greatly dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered and Dao Lian was killed, but Jishu climbed over the wall to surrender, and the rebel party fell apart.

sentences.zh: 乃四面進攻，沖車所沖，輒三五丈崩落。

translations.literal: Thereupon they attacked from four sides; wherever the battering ram struck, three to five zhang of wall would collapse.
translations.idiomatic: They then assaulted from all sides; wherever the battering ram struck, whole sections of wall thirty or fifty feet long crumbled away.

sentences.zh: 時南門樓上擲下一級，並垂繩釣取外人，外人上，賊並放仗，雲向已斬順則，所投首是也。

translations.literal: At that time from the south gate tower they lowered a ladder and also hung ropes to fish up outsiders; when outsiders came up, the rebels all laid down their weapons, saying they had already beheaded Shunze and that the head thrown down was his.
translations.idiomatic: From the south gate tower they lowered a rope ladder to haul people up. When men entered, the rebels laid down their arms, claiming Shunze was already dead and that the head they threw down was his.

sentences.zh: 秦凱之走河北。

translations.literal: Qin Kaizhi fled to the north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Kaizhi fled north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 斌坐滑臺退敗，免官。

translations.literal: Bin, on account of the withdrawal and defeat at Huatai, was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was dismissed for the failed siege and withdrawal from Huatai.

sentences.zh: 久之，復起為南平王鑠右軍長史。

translations.literal: After a long while he was again raised as Right Army Chief Clerk to Prince Nanping Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was reappointed right-army chief clerk to Prince Nanping Liu Shuo.

sentences.zh: 其後事蹟在《二凶傳》。

translations.literal: His later deeds are in the "Biographies of the Two Fiends."
translations.idiomatic: His later career is recorded in the "Biographies of the Two Fiends."

sentences.zh: 斌弟簡，歷位長沙內史。

translations.literal: Bin's younger brother Jian held the post of Interior Secretary of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's younger brother Jian served as interior secretary of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王誕為廣州，未之鎮，以簡為安南諮議參軍、南海太守，行府州事。

translations.literal: When Prince Guangling Dan was assigned to Guangzhou but had not yet gone to his post, Jian was made Pacifying South Adviser Staff Officer and Administrator of Nanhai, acting for the princely establishment and province.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Guangling Liu Dan was appointed to Guangzhou but had not yet taken up the post, Jian was made pacifying-south adviser and administrator of Nanhai, acting in his stead for the princedom and province.

sentences.zh: 東海王禕代誕，簡仍為前軍諮議，太守如故。

translations.literal: When Prince Donghai Yi replaced Dan, Jian remained Forward Army Adviser, administrator as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Donghai Liu Yi replaced Dan, Jian remained forward-army adviser and kept his post as administrator.

sentences.zh: 世祖入討元兇，遣輔國將軍、南海太守劉琬討簡，固守經時，城陷伏誅。

translations.literal: When the Shizu entered to suppress the usurper, he sent Assisting State General and Administrator of Nanhai Liu Wan to attack Jian; Jian held firm for a long time, the city fell, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Xiaowu marched to suppress the usurper, he sent Assisting State General and Nanhai administrator Liu Wan against Jian. Jian held out for a long time, but when the city fell he was executed.

sentences.zh: 斌、簡諸子並誅滅。

translations.literal: The sons of Bin and Jian were all executed to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Bin and Jian were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 劉延孫，彭城呂人，雍州刺史道產子也。

translations.literal: Liu Yansun was a man of Lü in Pengcheng, son of Yong Inspector Liu Daochan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yansun, a native of Lü in Pengcheng, was the son of Liu Daochan, inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 初為徐州主簿，舉秀才，彭城王義康司徒行參軍，尚書都官郎，為錢唐令，世祖撫軍、廣陵王誕北中郎中兵參軍、南清河太守。

translations.literal: He first served as Xu province chief clerk, was recommended as Presented Scholar, Staff Officer of the Minister over the Masses under Prince Pengcheng Yikang, Gentleman of the Ministry of Justice's Punishments Section, was made Magistrate of Qiantang, and served the Shizu as Pacifying Army and Prince Guangling Dan's North Central Army Central Troops Staff Officer and Administrator of Southern Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He began as chief clerk of Xu province, was recommended as presented scholar, served as staff officer to Prince Pengcheng under the minister over the masses, as gentleman in the ministry of justice's punishments section, and as magistrate of Qiantang. He later served the future Emperor Xiaowu as pacifying-army staff officer and central troops aide to Prince Guangling, and as administrator of Southern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 世祖為徐州，補治中從事史。

translations.literal: When the Shizu was in Xu province, he was appointed Acting Supervisor Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When the future emperor held Xu province, Yansun was made acting supervisor clerk.

sentences.zh: 時索虜圍縣瓠，分軍送所掠民口在汝陽，太祖詔世祖遣軍襲之，議者舉延孫為元帥，固辭無將用，舉劉泰之自代。

translations.literal: At that time the Northern Wei barbarians besieged Xuanchi and sent a detached army escorting captured common people at Ruyang. The Taizu ordered the Shizu to dispatch troops to raid them; those in council nominated Yansun as commander-in-chief, but he firmly declined for lack of generalship and recommended Liu Taizhi to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei besieged Xuanchi and sent a detachment escorting captives through Ruyang, the Taizu ordered the prince to strike them. The council nominated Yansun as commander, but he declined on the ground that he was no general and recommended Liu Taizhi in his place.

sentences.zh: 泰之既行，太祖大怒，免延孫官。

translations.literal: Once Taizhi had set out, the Taizu was greatly angered and dismissed Yansun from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizhi marched, the Taizu was furious and dismissed Yansun.

sentences.zh: 為世祖鎮軍北中郎中兵參軍，南中郎諮議參軍，領錄事。

translations.literal: He became the Shizu's Pacifying Army North Central Army Central Troops Staff Officer, South Army Adviser Staff Officer, and concurrently Chief Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed central troops aide on the pacifying army staff, south-army adviser, and chief recorder.

sentences.zh: 世祖伐逆，府缺上佐，轉補長史、尋陽太守，行留府事。

translations.literal: When the Shizu campaigned against the usurper, the establishment lacked a chief aide; he was transferred to fill the post of Chief Clerk and Administrator of Xunyang, acting for the remaining establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince marched against the usurper, his headquarters lacked a chief aide; Yansun was made chief clerk and administrator of Xunyang, acting for the rear establishment.

sentences.zh: 三年，南兗州刺史竟陵王誕有罪，不受徵，延孫馳遣中兵參軍杜幼文率兵起討。

translations.literal: In the third year the Inspector of Southern Yan, Prince Jingling Dan, was guilty and did not accept the summons; Yansun urgently sent Central Troops Staff Officer Du Youwen leading troops to raise punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his reign, Prince Jingling Liu Dan, inspector of Southern Yan, was charged with a crime and refused the summons. Yansun at once sent central troops aide Du Youwen with an army against him.

sentences.zh: 既至，誕已閉城自守，乃還。

translations.literal: Once they arrived, Dan had already shut the city and held himself in defense, so they returned.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they arrived, Dan had already shut the gates and held the city, so they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 誕遣使劉公泰齎書要之，延孫斬公泰，送首京邑。

translations.literal: Dan sent envoy Liu Gongtai bearing a letter to win him over; Yansun beheaded Gongtai and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent Liu Gongtai with a letter to win him over. Yansun beheaded Gongtai and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 復遣幼文率軍渡江，受沈慶之節度。

translations.literal: He again sent Youwen leading troops across the river, subject to Shen Qingzhi's command.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Youwen across the Yangzi under Shen Qingzhi's command.

sentences.zh: 其年，進號車騎將軍，加散騎常侍，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: That year he was advanced in title to General of Chariots and Cavalry, given the additional post of Regular Attendant-at-Large, and granted one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was promoted to general of chariots and cavalry, made regular attendant-at-large, and granted a military band.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔延孫曰：「舊京樹親，由來常準。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict to Yansun said, "The old capital's planting of kin has from of old been the constant standard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of his reign an edict to Yansun read: "It has always been the rule to place kinsmen in charge of the old capital.

sentences.zh: 卿前出所有別議，今此防久弭，當以還授小兒。

translations.literal: Your earlier departure had a separate discussion; now that this defense has long been quieted, it should be returned and given to my young son.
translations.idiomatic: When you left, other arrangements were made; now that the frontier has long been quiet, the post should go back to my son.

sentences.zh: 」徵延孫為侍中、尚書左僕射，領護軍將軍。

translations.literal: " Yansun was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, and concurrently General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: " Yansun was summoned to court as attendant-in-ordinary, left vice minister of the masters of writing, and general of the guards.

sentences.zh: 延孫疾病，不任拜起，上使於五城受封版，乘船自青谿至平昌門，仍入尚書下舍。

translations.literal: Yansun was ill and could not perform the bowing and rising; the sovereign had him receive the seal and commission at Wucheng, take a boat from Qingxi to Pingchang Gate, and then enter the lower quarters of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun was too ill to perform the obeisances. The emperor had him receive his commission at Wucheng, brought him by boat from Qingxi to Pingchang Gate, and lodged him in the ministry's guest quarters.

sentences.zh: 又欲以代朱脩之為荊州，事未行，明年，卒，時年五十二。

translations.literal: The sovereign also wished to have him replace Zhu Xiuzhi in Jing province; the matter had not been carried out when the next year he died, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also meant to appoint him Jing inspector in place of Zhu Xiuzhi, but before this could be done Yansun died the following year, at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 上甚惜之，下詔曰：「故侍中尚書左僕射、領護軍將軍東昌縣開國侯延孫，風局簡正，體識沈明，綢繆心膂，自蕃升朝，契闊唯舊，幾將二紀。

translations.literal: The sovereign greatly regretted it and issued an edict saying, "The late Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, and General of the Guards, Marquis of Dongchang County, Yansun—his bearing and conduct were simple and upright, his substance and insight deep and clear. He bound close to the heart and spine, rising from the princedom to court; our long intimacy is of old, nearly two reign periods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned him and issued an edict: "The late attendant-in-ordinary, left vice minister, and general of the guards, Marquis of Dongchang, Yansun, was upright in bearing and clear in judgment. Close to my heart since his days in my princedom, he has been my companion for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 靈業中圮，則首贊宏圖；

translations.literal: When the imperial enterprise collapsed midway, he was first to assist the great plan;
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial cause was shattered, he was the first to support my great design;

sentences.zh: 義令既舉，則任均蕭、寇。

translations.literal: once righteous command was raised, his charge equaled that of Xiao and Kou.
translations.idiomatic: when the righteous banner was raised, his responsibility matched that of Xiao He and Kou Xun.

sentences.zh: 器允棟幹，勳實佐時。

translations.literal: His capacity sufficed for a pillar and ridgepole; his merit truly assisted the age.
translations.idiomatic: His talent was that of a pillar of state, and his merit truly aided the times.

sentences.zh: 及累司馬兩官，出內尹牧，惠政茂課，著自民聽，忠謨令節，簡乎朕心。

translations.literal: When he repeatedly held the two offices of marshal, went out and in as capital governor and regional shepherd, his benevolent government and abundant achievements were manifest in the people's hearing; his loyal counsel and fine integrity were plain to Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: Whether serving twice as chief of staff, governing the capital, or shepherding the provinces, his benevolent rule won the people's praise, and his loyal counsel won my heart.

sentences.zh: 方燮和臺階，永毗國道，奄至薨殞，震慟兼深。

translations.literal: Just as he was to harmonize the terrace steps and forever assist the state's way, suddenly he reached death—Our shock and grief are both deep.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was to bring harmony to the court and long support the realm, he died suddenly, and my shock and grief are profound.

sentences.zh: 考終定典，宜盡哀敬。

translations.literal: Examining the end and fixing the rites, full mourning and respect are fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Let the rites of mourning be performed with full honor.

sentences.zh: 可贈司徒，給班劍二十人，侍中、僕射、侯如故。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously awarded Minister over the Masses, given twenty guards bearing swords, attendant, vice minister, and marquis as before.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously made minister over the masses, granted twenty sword-bearing guards, and retain his titles as attendant, vice minister, and marquis.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏諡忠穆，詔為文穆。

translations.literal: " The relevant offices memorialized the posthumous name Zhongmu; an edict changed it to Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: " The relevant offices proposed the posthumous name Loyal and Solemn; the emperor changed it to Cultured and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「故司徒文穆公延孫，居身寡約，家素貧虛，每念清美，良深淒歎。

translations.literal: Another edict said, "The late Minister Wenmu, Yansun, lived in few wants, his household always poor and empty; whenever We recall his pure excellence, Our sighs are truly deep.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict read: "The late Minister Cultured and Solemn, Yansun, lived simply and his household was always poor. When I recall his integrity, I am deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 葬送資調，固當闕乏，可賜錢三十萬，米千斛。」

translations.literal: Funds for burial and sending-off will certainly be lacking; he may be granted three hundred thousand cash and a thousand hu of grain."
translations.idiomatic: His funeral expenses will surely fall short. Grant him three hundred thousand cash and a thousand hu of grain."

sentences.zh: 子質嗣，太宗泰始中，有罪，國除。

translations.literal: His son Zhi succeeded; in the Taizong's Taishi era he was guilty and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi succeeded him, but in the Taishi era under Emperor Ming he was convicted and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 延孫弟延熙，義興太守，在孔覬傳。

translations.literal: Yansun's younger brother Yanxi was Administrator of Yixing; his account is in Kong Xian's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun's younger brother Yanxi, administrator of Yixing, is treated in Kong Xian's biography.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：延孫接款蕃日，固出顏、袁矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Yansun's reception of favor in princedom days was certainly above Yan and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In the days when Yansun won favor in the princedom, he was already above men like Yan and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 風飆局力，又無等級可言，而隆名盛寵，必擇而後授，何哉？

translations.literal: In wind and storm his scope of power had no rank to speak of, yet lofty name and abundant favor were always chosen before being bestowed—why?
translations.idiomatic: In talent and force he could not be ranked with the greatest ministers, yet the highest honors were always carefully chosen before they were granted him. Why?

sentences.zh: 良以休運甫開，沈疾方被，雖宿恩內積，而安私外簡。

translations.literal: Truly because the flourishing fortune had just opened and deep illness was just spreading—though old favor accumulated within, outwardly he was simple in settling private matters.
translations.idiomatic: Because the new dynasty was just rising and the emperor was often ill: though old affection ran deep within, outwardly Yansun kept his private life spare.

sentences.zh: 夫侮因事狎，敬由近疏，疏必相思，狎必相厭，厭思一殊，榮禮自隔，遂得為一世宗臣，蓋由此也。

translations.literal: Disrespect arises from familiarity through affairs; respect arises from nearness and distance. Distance necessarily produces mutual longing; familiarity necessarily produces mutual weariness. Weariness and longing once differ, glory and rites naturally separate—thus he could become a minister revered for an age; it was roughly from this.
translations.idiomatic: Familiarity breeds contempt, while distance breeds respect. Distance breeds longing, familiarity breeds weariness. Once weariness and longing diverge, honor and ritual keep their proper distance—and so he could stand for a generation as a minister of the first rank. This, in sum, was why.

sentences.zh: 子曰：「事君數，斯疏矣。

translations.literal: The Master said, "In serving one's lord, if one is frequent, one becomes distant.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "If in serving your lord you are too forward, you will earn his distance."

sentences.zh: 」然乎！

translations.literal: " Is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: " Is it not so!

sentences.zh: 然乎！

translations.literal: Is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: Is it not so!
